_source.describes: Host objects a settlement is built in, on or around
_source.status: House rule, assembled from SRD source material.
_source.rationale: The SRD says mouse settlements are "no more than a handful of families in an oak hollow or in an old farmhouse wall", and its hex Landmark tables supply the human-scale objects a settlement can occupy. Those landmark names are SRD text (CC BY 4.0); the shape, footprint and layout metadata attached to each is this project's invention, added to drive map generation.
_source.licence: Landmark names from the Mausritter SRD (CC BY 4.0). Metadata is original work by the mausritter-tools authors.
_source.attribution: This work is based on Mausritter (https://mausritter.com), a product of Losing Games and Isaac Williams, and is licensed for use under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence.
_source.warning: Safe to edit by hand. Unlike the files in ../srd/, this is not regenerated by the importer.

designNote: A Mausritter settlement should read as one human-scale object annotated at mouse scale, not as a village on open ground. The Third Party Licence's own guidance is to 'make it small and dense'. Each host below therefore describes a bounded container the map is drawn inside.

shapes.hollow: Rounded, organic interior. Roads spiral inward.
shapes.linear: Long and thin. One main road, buildings stacked along both faces.
shapes.vessel: Rounded body with a narrow mouth or spout. One entrance, dense interior.
shapes.boxy: Rectilinear human artefact. Grid-ish roads, hard outer edge.
shapes.warren: Branching underground network. Tunnels rather than streets.
shapes.sprawl: Open ground around a central feature. Loose, rambling roads.

hosts.name: Hollow tree stump
hosts.description: Ring of chambers carved into the rot-soft heartwood, with a chimney of daylight overhead.

hosts.name: Old farmhouse wall
hosts.description: Generations of mice living in the cavity between lath and plaster.

hosts.name: Old craggy oak
hosts.description: Halls in the trunk, storerooms in the roots, lookouts in the canopy.

hosts.name: Cow skeleton
hosts.description: Ribs as rafters, the skull repurposed as the grandest building for miles.

hosts.name: Dry stone wall
hosts.description: A settlement threaded through the gaps between stacked stones.

hosts.name: Massive fallen tree
hosts.description: A single long gallery running the length of the trunk, branching into the boughs.

hosts.name: Abandoned rabbit warren
hosts.description: Tunnels widened and shored up, the old owners long gone or politely displaced.

hosts.name: Drainpipe outlet
hosts.description: Dry in summer, evacuated in autumn. Everyone knows the drill.

hosts.name: Abandoned car
hosts.description: Seat foam for bedding, the engine bay for the forge, the boot for the granary.

hosts.name: Woodshed
hosts.description: A stacked city of split logs, rearranged every winter by giants.

hosts.name: Pile of trash
hosts.description: Endlessly renewed, endlessly picked over, and richer than it looks.

hosts.name: Dumped furniture
hosts.description: A sideboard tipped on its back, drawers become storeys.

hosts.name: Shopping trolley
hosts.description: Half-sunk in silt, the basket lashed over with woven grass.

hosts.name: Upturned boot
hosts.description: Sole for a roof, laceholes for windows, and a permanent smell nobody mentions.

hosts.name: Cracked teapot
hosts.description: The spout is the front gate. The lid is the council chamber.

hosts.name: Stone bridge
hosts.description: Built into the arch, above the waterline. Usually.

hosts.name: Sunken barge
hosts.description: Listing, half-flooded, and defended fiercely by those who live in the dry half.

hosts.name: Termite-riddled tree
hosts.description: Someone else's tunnels, inherited and hastily reinforced.

hosts.name: Huge flat rock
hosts.description: A roof of stone over a wide, dry, permanently twilit plaza.

hosts.name: Greenhouse
hosts.description: Warm, damp, and overgrown. Food grows year-round and so does everything else.

hosts.name: Blackberry hedge
hosts.description: Thorn walls no predator will push through, and a harvest that arrives on its own.

hosts.name: Trash-filled skip
hosts.description: Steel walls, no predators, and the constant terror of being emptied.
